name: Game Maker
description: Describe a game or hand it a design doc, and get a complete, playable game as an exhibit.
briefPlaceholder: Describe the game — genre, goal, controls, and look & feel. Or point at a design document and let it build from that...
promptScaffold:
This job produces a PLAYABLE GAME exhibit.
- Build a complete, self-contained, playable game from the user's description or referenced game design document.
- Implement real game logic: clear objective, win/lose conditions, scoring or progression, and responsive controls (keyboard and/or mouse/touch, whichever fits the genre).
- Include a start screen, an in-game HUD (score, lives, timer — whatever applies), and a game-over / restart flow. Support pause/resume.
- When a game design document is provided, follow it faithfully — mechanics, rules, theme, and content. Fill small gaps sensibly and list any assumptions in a short 'About' panel.
- Use canvas or DOM as fits the genre and keep it performant.
- No external assets or network calls: generate all visuals and audio with shapes, CSS, SVG, canvas, or the Web Audio API so the game runs fully offline.
- Follow the appended Gauntlet Loop protocol. Do not treat the first playable build as complete.

options.label: Design document
options.prompt: The game design is in this local file: {value} — read it and implement the game it describes. It may be .md, .txt, or .docx; for .docx, extract its text first (it is a zipped XML package — read word/document.xml).
